# ARCH-18: Data crosses from a driver's thread to the main loop only at the frontend's copy

- Sensor drivers split into a backend, whose periodic callback runs on the device's bus thread, and a frontend that runs in the main loop. The callback reads the device and writes only the backend's own accumulators, under the backend's semaphore (`_sem`). The frontend's `update()` calls the backend's `update()` or `read()`, which takes the same semaphore, copies the accumulated data into the frontend's state and resets it.
- That copy is the synchronisation point: the frontend's state, and everything downstream of it - AHRS, the EKF, the vehicle - is read and written only on the main thread (the shared-data line of [ARCH-9](ARCH-9.md)). A callback never calls out of its backend into the frontend or another library, and code that adds state on a path a callback can reach first checks which thread runs it. The BMP280 barometer (`_timer()` accumulates, `update()` copies out with `_copy_to_frontend()`), the VL53L1X range finder and the HereFlow flow driver (a `new_data` flag set in the callback, published from `update()`) keep this. Not every driver does yet: PulsedLightLRF writes the frontend's state from its I2C callback, Pixart reads the AHRS gyro in its, the compass publishes its raw field from the bus thread, and PX4Flow called `_update_frontend()` from its timer, which ran the EKF and the Replay logging on the bus thread ([#33484](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/33484)).

Confirmed 2026-10-16. Part of the root playbook, under [Architectural Principles](../claude/CLAUDE.md#architectural-principles). [All architectural rules](../README.md#architectural-rules)
